coverage.evidence: dashboard/src/layouts/dashboard/navigation.ts:59-60 gives each sidebar entry an action key, and dashboard/src/layouts/dashboard/useNavigation.ts:77-80 hides an entry when access.can(needed) is false, which supports the role-filtered sidebar. navigation.ts:176-183 puts Commands in the 'build' group, labeled Build and Commands in dashboard/src/i18n/locales/en.json:832 and 936. The bot is the chat-side sender in server/src/NomNomzBot.Infrastructure/Chat/HelixChatProvider.cs:389-414.

server/src/NomNomzBot.Api/Controllers/V1/AuthController.cs:408-422 sends every role except Broadcaster (moderator and viewer) to the 'viewer' flow. server/src/NomNomzBot.Infrastructure/Identity/AuthService.cs:340-389 (HandleTwitchViewerCallbackAsync) writes only the User row and opens a session with no channel, or keeps the arriving channel of the same user; no channel is created and nothing is onboarded. The labels Continue as broadcaster and Continue as moderator are in dashboard/src/views/site/login/i18n/en.json:24-25.

AuthService.cs:643-665 publishes ChannelOnboardedEvent as fire-and-forget on every streamer sign-in. server/src/NomNomzBot.Infrastructure/Community/EventHandlers/ModeratorRosterSeedOnOnboardingHandler.cs:20-47 handles it with SyncModeratorsFromTwitchAsync, which copies the Twitch moderator roster into ChannelModerators. PermissionService.cs:71 then reads ChannelModerators as the moderator role.

server/src/NomNomzBot.Infrastructure/Identity/ChannelService.cs:278-284 returns channels where OwnerUserId matches, or Moderators.Any(m.UserId), or the extra Twitch ids. server/src/NomNomzBot.Api/Controllers/V1/ChannelsController.cs:112-120 fills those extra ids (moderatedIds) only when ResolveOwnChannelAsync finds an own channel, so the list is empty for a moderator who owns none. dashboard/src/layouts/dashboard/ChannelSwitch.vue:54-77 shows those rows under 'Channels you moderate' (en.json:982), and DashboardSidebar.vue:38-39 puts the switcher in the SidebarHeader.

The license header in ModeratorRosterSeedOnOnboardingHandler.cs:4-6 reads 'You may use, change and share it for free, for any noncommercial purpose ... You may not earn money with it.' The starting paths come from docker-compose.lite.yml:42 (Deployment__Mode=self_host_lite) and docker-compose.yml for self-hosting, plus sign-in to an existing installation.

reader_answers.evidence: The steps match the source. AuthService.cs:527-566 creates and onboards the broadcaster channel. Commands sits in the Build group per navigation.ts:176-183 and en.json:936. The schedule command is answered in chat, and OfflineCommandGate.cs:25-27 lets the broadcaster's own test through while offline.

The two needs match the source: Docker per docker-compose.lite.yml, and a Twitch app that is either your own (TWITCH_CLIENT_ID at docker-compose.lite.yml:49) or the shipped public client id (AuthService.cs:574-576, SystemController.cs:73). Sign-in is with Twitch per LoginView.vue:131-149. A moderator needs the broadcaster's sign-in first because only it fires the roster seed (AuthService.cs:643-665).

Broadcaster sign-in onboards the channel (AuthService.cs:561-566), and Channel.Enabled defaults to true (Channel.cs:69), so the bot joins. When no own bot and no shared bot exists, the sender falls back to the owner's account (HelixChatProvider.cs:411-414), so the reply shows under the streamer's name.

The moderator path in the answer matches the source. Moderator sign-in opens a session with no channel and never onboards one (AuthController.cs:410-422, AuthService.cs:340-389). Access comes from the ChannelModerators row seeded by the broadcaster's sign-in (ModeratorRosterSeedOnOnboardingHandler.cs:44-47, ChannelService.cs:278-284), and the channel appears under 'Channels you moderate' (ChannelSwitch.vue:76-77).
